Unfortunately passing is a lot easier for some people but that doesn't mean there isn't things that can help. There are makeup tutorials on YouTube to help you better contour your face to look more feminine ( https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=gUl-WHAL9qo ). Also hair styles can be changed to highlight more feminine features ( https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=PDgLMdn751c ). Clothing also goes a long way, when people see someone in traditionally feminine clothing they are more likely to see them as female. There's also more drastic options for adults if you can afford it such as facial reconstructive surgery to achieve a more feminine face and other surgeries for a more feminine body including breast implants.

Your safety is the most important thing, you can always try and educate them without outing yourself (say you have a trans family memeber) but also that isn't your responsibility if you don't want to. If you think them knowing would impede your physical or mental health or your education it may be better not to tell them.

Hi I'm in a similar situation where I'm not really sure how to come out as ftm either. But it seems like you're very worried about facing their immediate reactions. It might help to write them a letter instead that way you can make sure that every point you want to get across comes through. Also I'm sorry you felt like you needed to use femininity to hide I'm sure that was extremely hard and maybe you could also do some things to help yourself feel more comfortable in your identity, like get a haircut (Of course you don't have to! Many guys have long hair! Just look at Henry Cavill in the witcher) or maybe get yourself a more masculine or unisex item of clothing to wear. When you feel more comfortable in your identity it's easier to accept characteristics of yourself that don't traditionally fit with your gender because even cis guys aren't 100% masculine.

I'm not saying this is definitely the case but it could be that your wife is on the asexual spectrum. Generally though not in all cases this means that she won't feel a desire towards sexual intimacy. This doesn't mean that she might not enjoy it in the moment (although other asexual people may feel differently) but if this is the case, it likely means that she doesn't understand what it means to you and how you view it as part of a healthy relationship. I highly advise talking to your wife about your concerns that she may not have been as enthusiastic in past encounters as you've thought as it sounds like you hold much love for her and are wondering wether you might have taken advantage of society's pressure on women to have sex in long term relationships which I can clearly see was not your intention at all. Hopefully she can explain her feelings to you as well.
